claims.rawValue: Weight allowance adjusts the normal unencumbered allowance, measured in gold-piece weight (10 gp = 1 lb). Parenthesized door chances are out of six for fighters forcing locked, barred, magically held or wizard-locked doors: only one attempt per door is allowed. Bend-bars/lift-gates attempts are also one-time attempts.
One gold piece equals 20 silver pieces, 200 copper pieces or 2 electrum pieces. One platinum piece equals 5 gold pieces.
Below name level, standard weekly cost is the current level × 1,500 gp.

At name level, characters train or study independently for the performance-determined time; weekly cost per level is 2,000 gp for clerics, 1,000 for fighters, 4,000 for magic-users, and 2,000 for thieves.

Bards contribute at least 50% of monetary gains plus 1,000 gp per level upon advancement to their college, through a druid able to use more of their highest-level spells than the bard; failure to pay prevents advancement. They otherwise need one week of study or training upon gaining sufficient XP.
Restoring each point of absorption costs 100 gp and one day with a trained armorer.
Repair costs 200 gp and two days for each absorption point restored.
Daily / monthly pay: bearer or porter 1 sp / 1 gp; carpenter 3 sp / 2 gp; leather worker 2 sp / 30 sp; limner 10 sp / 10 gp; linkboy 1 sp / 1 gp.
Mason 4 sp / 3 gp; pack handler 2 sp / 30 sp; tailor 2 sp / 30 sp; teamster 5 sp / 5 gp; valet or lackey 3 sp / 50 sp.

Treasure can distract pursuers of low intelligence or higher: start at 10%–100%, adding 10% per 10 items for low-intelligence pursuers or 10% per 100 gp of value or potential value for those of average intelligence or more. Test with a second d10; success lasts one round or the time needed to collect the treasure, whichever is longer. Tiny valuables can go unnoticed.

claims.rawValue: PHB p. 19, Table II: any armor, shield, or weapon; oil is allowed and poison is referee-dependent. The any*** row restricts characters under 5 ft. from longbows or weapons over 12 ft., and characters under 100 lb. from heavy crossbows or pole arms over 200 gp weight (including two-handed swords).

PHB p. 19, Table II: any armor, shield, or weapon; oil is allowed; poison is never allowed. The any*** row restricts characters under 5 ft. from longbows or weapons over 12 ft., and characters under 100 lb. from heavy crossbows or pole arms over 200 gp weight (including two-handed swords).

PHB p. 19, Table II: any armor, shield, or weapon; oil is allowed and poison is referee-dependent. The any*** row restricts characters under 5 ft. from longbows or weapons over 12 ft., and characters under 100 lb. from heavy crossbows or pole arms over 200 gp weight (including two-handed swords).

PHB p. 19, Table II: leather armor, any shield or weapon; oil and poison are allowed. The any*** row restricts characters under 5 ft. from longbows or weapons over 12 ft., and characters under 100 lb. from heavy crossbows or pole arms over 200 gp weight (including two-handed swords).

UA p. 25 Tables II and III adjust the Acrobat’s base function chances or maxima for Strength and Dexterity; apply their stated racial adjustments as well. Table IV separates body-associated weight (clothing, accessories, armor, weapons) from additional carried weight, which applies only while tightrope walking; backpacks are otherwise barred during Acrobat activities. Its level-14 extra 1,000 gp and level-22 passenger examples are limited by the accompanying procedure.

contextRegionCoverage.interpretation: Annotated counts identify reviewed contract coverage; containment passes and clipped results are reported separately. Unannotated regions are not-assessable, not passed.

continuationCoverage.scope: Source-bound excerpt segments for reviewed Charging, Abjure, the shared PHB p.33 human two-class example, the shared PHB p.70 Invisibility passage, the UA p.10 elven-subrace passage, and the UA p.59–60 Magic-User Contingency passage. Records distinguish printed-page order from PDF source identity. The twelve p.33 groups preserve the same-page left-to-right opening/continuation for ten core class catalogs, the dual-class rule, and progression explainer. These groups assert source-image passage parts and order only; mechanics, values, owner-specific field support, variant applicability, and precise highlights remain pending. Unlisted continuations remain unassessed. The 38 DMG p.225 encumbrance groups link each complete table row to the same-page right-column exclusion and bulkiness continuation in bottom-left to top-right order; source values and owner-specific mechanics remain separate reviews. The two Drow page10–11 groups preserve primary and legacy crop variants of the same cross-page passage; available context is linked but the original fold/shadow and fact highlights remain unresolved. This unpublished candidate appends ten accepted UA source-context joins to the exact 261-group weapon branch prefix; it is prospective and is not the live cc950 base manifest.

semanticReviewUniverse.scope: Sparse rule and pointer-index mapping over every JSON node rooted in every exposed content record. Each listed obligation dimension defaults to unresolved/not-assessable; exact annotations are surfaced as scoped overrides, never expanded to unrelated properties.

pointerIndex.selectionRule: Include a tuple when its JSON Pointer equals or descends from any recordPointers[].pointer. This preserves an exact pointer for every node without duplicating dimension status on each tuple.

pinnedGitBaselineComparators.interpretation: These are distinct denominators. The 4,820 explicit field/price slots are a narrower UI-target subset, not all 13,193 mechanics-audit fields or all 34,280 scalar/null leaves.

semanticReviewUniverse.inventoryClassMeaning: Node classes are syntactic inventory categories. A metadata or citation-metadata node marked not-assessable says nothing about whether its name, label, or fact is semantically correct. No node-level class is a semantic source verification.

structuralValidation.scope: Fails only for confirmed structural owner/catalog/region/page/source-object joins. Pending semantic review, empty targets, explicitly unmapped candidate IDs, context/qualifier incompleteness, full-image sentinels, and unannotated obligations remain visible but do not fail this structural gate.

sourceVisualCoverage.reason: Not run in in-memory test mode.

limitations: A confirmed node inventory class, JSON pointer, or catalog target means only that the recorded structure resolves; it does not prove the cited passage supports the value or that a name/label is semantically correct.
Money-like string matching is intentionally broad and keeps exact raw text; currency candidates are not all prices. XP, weights, package counts and prose may still require a human to classify.
Region IDs resolve only in the exact catalog selected by sourceExcerpts || scanVerification on the source owner. No cross-catalog fallback is attempted.
Only explicitly annotated context, continuation, and qualifier requirements have structural checks. Unannotated obligations are not-assessable, not passed.
Geometry checks and recorded visual reviews are reused as evidence from the existing source-visual-coverage API; they do not establish source completeness or semantic accuracy.

reloadResolution.exactCrops: not assessed by this failure fixture; no region geometry is introduced or inferred

observedGaps.repro: Build and attach price inventory in-memory; `phb-bo-stick` comparison 0 produces `/suggestedPrice/comparisons/0` with `sourceOwner=equipment:phb-spear`. `FirstEditionCitations.targets(comparison)` omits sourceOwner. The direct click is contextualized to phb-spear, and on reload app route searches that field pointer only in phb-spear targets, where it is absent. Current served dist/data.json has 662 field bindings while the current inventory builder validates 668, including six new comparator bindings; therefore the exact field-target round trip is not exercised by the current browser fixture. Existing browser assertion checks only that the reloaded viewer title is Spear; it does not assert field target identity/label, pending notice or exact target list.

Current viewer field-target browser test invokes FirstEditionSourceViewer.open() directly. Current app-level citation navigation unit test uses synthetic refs and source-function extraction; no browser test clicks an assembled equipment field target and then reloads that exact field URL.
The `Copy reference link` footer button copies only `#view/id`; no test asserts it or clarifies that it intentionally copies item-level rather than active source location.

Compact equipment/spell field-source layout emits inline chips, but spell table layout omits the source column (`attributeLayoutHTML` conditionally emits it only for equipment). No test verifies citations remain discoverable across compact/table toggles for spells.

Matrices are source-owner targets rather than root views. Existing tests cover fighter matrix context/reload, but no general page-only matrix route exists by design; sources/notebook pages have no source-navigation chip path tested beyond general app/accessibility tests.
